Menu Visit What’s on Explore the collection Help using the archive Education Professional guidance and services Search Shop Home Cookies on nationalarchives.gov.uk Cookies are small files saved on your phone, tablet or computer when you visit a website. We use cookies to collect and store information about how you use National Archives websites which means any page with nationalarchives.gov.uk in the URL. Success Your cookie settings were saved. This page has a brief explanation of each of the four types of cookie The National Archives uses. You can choose which cookies you’re happy for us to use. For a full breakdown, see our detailed cookie information . Cookie preferences We use 4 types of cookie. You can choose which cookies you’re happy for us to use. Cookies that measure website use We use Google Analytics cookies to measure how you use National Archives websites. These cookies collect information about: how you got to these sites the pages you visit and how long you spend on each page what you click on while you’re visiting these sites We do not allow Google to use or share this data for their own purposes. Do you allow cookies that measure website use? Use cookies that measure my website use Do not use cookies that measure my website use Cookies that help with our communications and marketing These cookies may be set by third party websites and do things like measure how you view YouTube videos that are on our websites. Do you allow cookies that help with communications and marketing? Use cookies that help with communications and marketing Do not use cookies that help with communications and marketing Cookies that remember your settings These cookies do things like remember your preferences and the choices you make, to personalise your experience of using the site. Do you allow cookies that remember your settings? Use cookies that remember my settings on the site Do not use cookies that remember my settings on the site Strictly necessary cookies These essential cookies do things like allow you to progress through a form or to remain logged in to some of our services. They always need to be on. Menu Visit What’s on Explore the collection Help using the archive Education Professional guidance and services Search Shop Home What's on Discover our exhibitions, events and family activities for all – online and at Kew. Everything that's on What's on today Next 7 days Next 30 days Talks and tours Join archives staff and world-leading experts for exciting talks and tours, in person and online. Tour Curator tour – Revolution 250: America's Independence Story 1763–1783 Cost £15 Date 13 October to 13 November 2026 Explore highlights from our current exhibition, Revolution 250 with curators Graham Moore and Sean Cunningham. Tour Behind the scenes tours Cost £20 Date 14 October to 17 December 2026 Take the chance to go behind the scenes at The National Archives' repositories and see a range of historical documents. Display Stories Unboxed Cost Free Date 2026 Each month we take a single, remarkable document, put it on display, and explore its story. Display The Cabinet Table Cost Free Date 2026 Examine our replica Cabinet table and explore leaders from the past through their documents. Display Hamilton at The National Archives Cost Free Date 10 June to 29 November 2026 Straight from London's West End, get closer to costumes from the hit musical Hamilton at The National Archives. Family activity Time Travel Tots: messy play Cost £5 Date 9 October to 4 December 2026 Join us for a messy play session! Menu Visit What’s on Explore the collection Help using the archive Education Professional guidance and services Search Shop Home Please note We are refreshing our teaching resources and regularly adding new and updated ones. All of our old resources are permanently available in the UK Government Web Archive . Dismiss notification Education We believe that school students should be given the same access to original documents as professional historians. Explore teaching resources developed with our records experts and discover our programme of education sessions and workshops held online, at The National Archives and around the country. Teaching resources All of our resources follow an enquiry-based approach and use records from our collections at The National Archives. Education sessions Our taught sessions for schools are offered free of charge. Whether online or in-person, they are all led by experts in history and education. Read more About education at The National Archives Learn about our approach to education, what to expect when you take part in one of our workshops and more of what we have to offer for teachers and students. Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) We offer a dedicated learning programme for students with special educational needs and disabilities. The National Archives education bursary schemes Bursaries are available to support visits to our headquarters in Kew and for visits to our North East partners at the Discovery Museum, Newcastle. We also provide a number of commercial services. Archive sector The National Archives holds leadership responsibilities for the archive sector in England. Find guidance on running an archive, apply for funding, and more. Caring for our collection We ensure access to The National Archives’ collection through its long-term preservation and display. Commercial services We offer a wide range of professional services from digitisation, licensing and publishing to heritage conservation, collection loans and venue hire.
